email_note: No public email found. Checked: Instagram bio and search-indexed bio text for @squirtin_ink, Facebook page (facebook.com/pages/Squirtin-Ink-Tattoo-Studio/111196508034851, not directly fetchable via curl with facebookexternalhit UA or WebFetch, both attempts returned no usable About/contact content), squirtinink.com (parked GoDaddy page, only a generic newsletter signup form, no business email), bestprosintown.com, tattooshoplocator.com, wanderboat.ai, roadtrippers listings, inked4lifetattoos.com/miami-squirtin-ink (third-party collective marketing page, no email listed). hours_note: Closed Mondays; Tuesday-Thursday 12pm-8pm; Friday-Sunday 12pm-10pm. Cross-verified consistently across roadtrippers.com (two separate listing pages: 'squirtin-ink' and 'squirtin-ink-tattoo-studio'), tattooshoplocator.com and general web search summaries. Not from a first-party bookable page (no own website or booking platform), so treated as reliable via cross-source agreement but not first-party-authoritative.
rating_source: Cross-aggregator consistency, NOT a single first-party citation. bestprosintown.com/fl/florida-city/squirtin-ink-/ and tattooshoplocator.com/shop/squirtin-ink-florida-city-florida both independently show '4.8 stars / 161 reviews' with no breakdown of which platform (Google, Yelp, etc.) the figure aggregates. Ran 3 additional searches specifically trying to find a more direct/first-party source (searched for a Birdeye page, searched 'Squirtin Ink tattoo Homestead Google reviews', searched 'Squirtin Ink birdeye.com reviews'): no Birdeye profile exists for this business, and no search snippet surfaced a Google Business Profile figure shown directly (e.g. a Google Maps snippet or Google-labeled star count). The 4.8/161 figure is used as the best available number given it independently agrees across two unrelated business-directory aggregators, but this is a materially weaker source than a direct Google/Yelp citation. No differing figure was found, so no change was made from the number provided in the task brief.
other_platform_note: Individual Yelp listings show much lower counts for the same address/phone (yelp.com/biz/squirtin-ink-homestead page metadata referenced only 1 fetchable review; a Roadtrippers page sourcing Yelp content shows 5 Yelp reviews with 3 shown in full). These are Yelp-only tallies, clearly a subset, not a contradiction of the 161 cross-platform total, just evidence Yelp alone carries far fewer of the 161.
own_site_check: squirtinink.com resolves and returns a live page, but it is a GoDaddy Website Builder placeholder: the page's only content is a repeated 'Launching Soon' heading, a generic email signup form ('Sign up for our email list for updates, promotions, and more'), and a 'Powered by GoDaddy' footer. No business name, services, photos, or contact info beyond the form. Re-confirmed via a fresh WebFetch on 2026-07-29 during this build. Treated as NOT a functional website; has_own_site is false.
instagram_note: @squirtin_ink, 7,812 followers, 2,101 posts (per task brief and corroborating search results, one search snapshot showed 2,619 following as a separate figure). Active, real account posting tattoo/piercing work, reels and shop updates. Individual artist handles seen tagged in posts: @chino_inks (matches reviewer-named artist 'Chino') and a 'chicom4l' handle suggesting an M4L ('Marked 4 Life' / Inked 4 Life collective) affiliation; not confirmed as an official brand claim, so not used as a marketing claim on the site.
facebook_note: URL provided in task brief. Could not retrieve page content: both a direct WebFetch and a curl fetch with a facebookexternalhit user agent returned no usable About/contact/photo content (Facebook served a JS-shell page with no populated meta tags in this environment). Listed on-site as a follow link only; no claims are made about its content beyond its existence.
collective_note: inked4lifetattoos.com/miami-squirtin-ink is a marketing page for this shop hosted on a third-party tattoo-collective domain ('Inked 4 Life Tattoo Collective', which operates multiple shops). This is NOT a first-party website owned by Squirtin' Ink (different domain, third-party network site), so it does not change has_own_site. It was used only as a research source for pricing-structure language ('shop minimum applies; larger pieces typically priced hourly') and generic style descriptors ('crisp linework', 'bold color bombs').

services_note: No fixed price list found anywhere (no own website, no booking platform with a price menu). The only pricing-structure statement found is on the third-party inked4lifetattoos.com/miami-squirtin-ink collective page: 'Pricing varies by size, complexity, and placement; shop minimum applies; larger pieces typically priced hourly.' No dollar figures given anywhere, so none are used on the site: all service cards use 'Free Consult / Quote at booking' or 'Shop Minimum / Larger pieces priced hourly' instead of invented numbers, per task instructions. Tattoo styles referenced on site (traditional, black and grey, color, script/lettering) are grounded directly in: (1) Sabrina B.'s verbatim review, 'caters to every style... whatever tattoo you want traditional, black and white', and (2) the real photo gallery itself (script lettering, color floral/animal pieces, blackwork). Piercing menu is grounded in a real first-party Instagram photo post by the business (a flyer titled 'PIERCING SERVICES - SQUIRTIN INK TATTOO STUDIO') listing: Ear Piercings (Lobes, Helix, Conch, Flat, Rook, Daith, Forward Helix, Snug, Antitragus, Tragus, Vertical Helix, Industrial), Nose & Facial Piercings (Nostril, Bridge, Eyebrow, Septum, Medusa), Oral & Lip Piercings (Labret, Snake Bites, Angel Fangs, Vertical Labret, Spider Bites, Jestrum, Tongue), Body Piercings (Navel/Belly, Nipples), Intimate Piercings (Genital Piercings, consult required), plus a note 'Surface Piercings & Dermals Coming Soon' and 'DM us with questions or to book'. Site's piercing service card only lists a representative subset (lobe, helix, conch, rook, tragus, daith, septum, nostril, eyebrow, oral, navel) to keep the card readable; nothing invented.

build_note: Derived from templates/dark-v2/index.html per templates/SKELETONS-V2.md. A pre-existing shared-template characteristic was found and safely mitigated: in the current Chromium build used for local verification, `.img-reveal` elements that are within the initial viewport can get IntersectionObserver ratio stuck at 0 (self clip-path on the observed element affecting the browser's own ratio calculation), so the reveal-in class is never added and the image stays permanently clipped/invisible. This was verified to reproduce identically on the already-shipped output/lakeside-grooming-tallahassee/index.html, so it is not specific to this build. A minimal, local-only defensive fallback was added to THIS site's script only (not to the shared templates/ files): a 2.6s timeout that force-adds the '.in' class to any '.reveal'/'.img-reveal' element that has not yet revealed, guaranteeing all real photos are always visible regardless of IntersectionObserver behavior in any given browser. Verified via Playwright: 60/60 reveal elements end up visible, no horizontal overflow at 390px viewport, ES/EN toggle works correctly.
